content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim against the evidence. The root cause points at render_spend_summary calling typical_spend_per_item when use_typical_spend is set, and F1 and U1 back that up. The Code-Fix reading of that function as a repeated scan for the middle price rests on F1 alone, so I'm treating it as unverified.

I'm going through the remaining claims one by one. The cause-in-plain-words point holds up: switching the flag on sent the shop down a slower path, and the latency rise lines up with that. I'm also checking the symptom figures, where the slowest requests went from about 198 to 1406, and the timing of the flag changes around 03:18 and 03:24.

I'm working through the remaining claims: the causal chain links the flag switch to the slowdown, the Code-Fix reading accounts for why long-history requests became slow, and the action items point at the same quadratic flag-off path.

I'm confirming that the alert didn't page anyone, and that the record supports that point.

supported.quote: With use_typical_spend true, render_spend_summary calls typical_spend_per_item (src/io_shop/typical_spend.py).
Code-Fix read that function as finding the middle price by repeatedly scanning the whole purchase history for its minimum and then scanning it again to remove it, many times over.
Its work therefore grows far faster than the history's length, so requests for shoppers with long histories pay a large cost. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

Switching on a feature made the shop use a new way of working out a shopper's typical spend, and that method likely slows down sharply for shoppers with a long purchase history, so their pages took much longer to load.
Switching typical-purchase-feature back on, or sending any other request to the typical-spend calculation, could again make requests for shoppers with long purchase histories very slow.
The slowest io-shop requests took far longer to load
The slowest requests to io-shop took far longer than usual. Its slowest-request latency rose from the minute the incident began, and no more requests failed than before.

Requests started going through the flag-on path when admin switched typical-purchase-feature on at {P1.1}. Before that, the service's flag evaluations were all off (Ga6f5). They were split during {Gc8c4.6} (Gc8c4) and all on from then until the alert (Gd44a).
Any other flag change: the flag provider's history showed no flag change by anyone but Argus other than this switch in the period read.
With the flag on, render_spend_summary calls typical_spend_per_item to build the shopper's spend summary.
Code-Fix read typical_spend_per_item's work as growing far faster than a shopper's purchase history, so requests for shoppers with long histories became slow.
Before typical-purchase-feature was switched on, no check was seen that measured the latency of the code path it enabled for shoppers with long purchase histories.
The flag was switched on for all traffic in one step: evaluations went from all off to all on almost immediately, and no gradual rollout was seen.
No test was seen that bounds how much work typical_spend_per_item does on a long purchase history.
The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
